chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Kufi, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Azrami, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

“A man was found with another man during the rule of 'Umar. One of the two fled, and the other was seized and brought to 'Umar. He said to the people, ‘What do you think?’” He said: “So one said, ‘Do this,’ and another said, ‘Do that.’” He said: “Then he said, ‘What do you say, O Aba al-Hasan?’” He said: “So he said, ‘Strike his neck.’ So his neck was struck.” He said: “Then he wanted to carry him away, so he عليه السلام said, ‘Wait, for there still remains something of his hadd.’” He said: “What thing remains?” He said: “‘Call for firewood.’ So 'Umar called for firewood, and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered concerning him, and he was burned with it.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَارَةِ: rule or governance under a political authority
key_terms.اِضْرِبْ عُنُقَهُ: strike his neck; an order for execution
key_terms.مَا تَرَوْنَ: what judgment or opinion you consider appropriate

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam narrate about Imam 'Ali’s عليه السلام judgment in the hadd of liwat during the rule of 'Umar?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident reported from Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام concerning a legal punishment carried out in the time of 'Umar, in which the judgment of أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام was sought. It reflects a juridical and historical report tied to the chapter on the hadd of liwat and highlights the authority of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in legal judgment.
